newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech state fund kills Prazska Energetika dividend.
newsitem.headline: Czech state fund kills Prazska Energetika dividend.

text.p: The Czech state-run National Property Fund (NPF) voted along with the city of Prague to block a proposal by Prague power distributor Prazska Energetika a.s. to pay out a 30 crown gross dividend per share on 1996 earnings.
"The proposal (for dividend) was not approved," Jan Dolezalek, the head of the firm's office, told Reuters.

The dividend proposal was widely expected to fail after the Czech Industry and Trade Ministry, which manages the state stakes in energy companies, said it would seek to block dividends on 1996 profit at all energy companies due to their modernisation needs.
The NPF holds a controlling stake in the company, and when combined with the votes from shares held by the city of Prague, has effectively an absolute majority.
The ministry has said it would be politically difficult to justify dividend payments at the time of energy price hikes for households.
The NPF has already blocked a proposal to pay out the first-ever dividend at the country's main power producer CEZ a.s.
Prazska Energetika paid out a 20 crown gross dividend on 1995 earnings. The company's net profit declined last year to 322 million crowns from 455 million crowns in 1995.
